newsitem.title: USA: Western Resources raises cash part of ADT bid.
newsitem.headline: Western Resources raises cash part of ADT bid.

text.p: ADT Ltd. Monday again rejected as inadequate a takeover offer by Western Resources Inc., the company's largest shareholder, after it raised the cash part of the bid by 33 percent to $10 per share from $7.50.
The overall value of Western's bid, launched in December, remains at $22.50 per share, or about $3.5 billion.

Western, a utility company based in Topeka, Kansas, said its offer now consists of $10 in cash and $12.50 in stock for each ADT share. The original offer was for $7.50 in cash and $15 in Western stock.
Western also said it would sell ADT's auto-auction business if successful in the acquisition, and expected to realise $450 million from the sale.

ADT, the largest electronic security services company in the United States and Britain, responded that it will recommend that shareholders reject the hostile offer as inadequate, as it does not reflect the inherent value of the company. Moreover, ADT said the actual value of Western's offer could be "significantly" lower than its stated value.
Western said it was disappointed by the rejection, but that it would move forward with its offer for the company.

ADT also said Western would not make a strong strategic partner and that the merger would offer no strategic opportunities for ADT or its shareholders. Instead, it would produce unacceptable risks for all ADT stakeholders, it said.

"We understand why a slow growth Kansas utility thinks it would benefit from buying a high growth international electronic security services company but fail to see any compelling reason why ADT shareholders would benefit from such an alliance," said ADT Chairman Michael Ashcroft.

ADT said its Security Services division is evolving into a company which gathers and distributes data for premises control services, and is positioning itself for significant growth in a rapidly changing industry.

ADT said it has scheduled a special general meeting for July 8 to vote on Western's proposals to replace its directors with ADT employees, and that it has filed a preliminary proxy statement opposing that proposal.
ADT, meanwhile, is suing Chase Manhattan Corp., alleging that Chase, an ADT lender, breached fiduciary duty by backing Western's bid.
Western's stock rose 25 cents to $30.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
